svg.title: Figure 4. Marine predictors improve retrospective island comparisons but show limited geographic transfer
svg.desc: Panel A, 51 held islands: ocean geometry beyond distance +5.08%, known host assemblages beyond AIS and wind +1.73%, AIS and wind beyond known hosts +6.49% reduction in mean squared error. These use different reference models and are not additive. Panel B, 990 geographically unseen pairs with retrospective host adjustment: AIS only +0.68%, AIS plus wind -4.70% MSE reduction. Negative means worse. The plot assesses indexed butterfly assemblages and does not infer shipping, dispersal or establishment.

g.text: Marine geography matters—but transfer is limited
Retrospective butterfly assemblage models • positive bars reduce prediction error
51 islands • relative mean-squared-error (MSE) reduction • different model baselines
These gains have different reference models; they must not be added together.
B. Both island endpoints geographically unseen
990 pair comparisons • later recorded butterflies • retrospective host-adjusted models
Negative reduction means worse predictions. AIS/wind are proxies, not movement tracks.
Panels differ in geography, holdout design and reference models; comparisons are descriptive.
No direct evidence of larval feeding, ship carriage, butterfly arrival or successful island establishment.
